subject: Reserved capacity regression — immediate coordination & exec ask
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nutribank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Oncall <sre+oncall@nutribank.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe degradation on reserved pool — NutriBank production

Aditya —

We started seeing a severe drop in throughput and a jump in 5xx errors against our reserved pool around 07:50 PDT. Latency doubled and many requests are timing out. Our SRE toggled fallback to a smaller model but we still see queueing and token backpressure. This is impacting checkout flows.

I attached the short tail logs and a snapshot of the token usage. Can you confirm whether this is a service-side saturation or something on our end? We need an ETA for mitigation — customers are noticing.

Attachments: nutribank_tail_logs_0428.tar.gz (text), reserved-usage-20270428.csv (csv)

— Elena
Elena Torres
Director, Platform Engineering
NutriBank
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@nutribank.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe degradation on reserved pool — NutriBank production

Thanks for flagging, Elena — sorry for the impact.

@Priyom / SRE: can you triage immediate root cause? NutriBank reports: sudden throughput drop, 5xx spike, queueing on their reserved capacity (deal D-87921). Logs attached by customer show repeated model-kv cache misses and token queue growth. Please check GPU headroom, slot saturation, and whether any autoscaler event or background maintenance coincided.

Jordan / Marissa: marking as high-priority customer-impacting ticket. If this is reserved-pool exhaustion we will likely need short-duration burst capacity or temporary routing to compatible fallback variants. Please advise on exec escalation and approved burst credit thresholds.

I'll collect triage notes and propose an immediate mitigation path.

— Aditya Rao
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@nutribank.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe degradation on reserved pool — NutriBank production

Quick triage summary (observed at 08:40 PDT):
- Cluster: us-west-2-dedicated-14 (NutriBank reserved group) shows sustained GPU utilization ~98% across the pool.
- Queue depth: user-queue for their reservation climbed from median 12 -> 220 requests.
- Error pattern: 502/504 spikes tied to timeout at our proxy layer when KV cache hits drop during model changeovers.
- Recent events: an internal kernel upgrade rolled to subset of nodes at 07:45 PDT; autoscaler did NOT trigger additional reserved nodes because reservation headroom policy is strict (no overcommit).

Immediate recommendations:
1) Open temporary burst capacity (enable reserved-burst for NutriBank + route excess to pre-approved burst nodes) — ETA to stand up: 12 min.
2) Apply conservative token-level rate-limit for their highest-volume route (checkout-api) to prevent queue collapse — ETA: 6 min.
3) Enable model-fallback to a slightly smaller variant with same API contract for 5–15% of traffic (gradual ramp) — ETA: 9 min.

I've uploaded a diagnostic bundle to our internal Ops playbook and attached a short CSV summary.

Attachments: reserved-usage-20270428.csv (derived), ops-diagnostics-nutribank-0428.tar.gz (internal)

— Priyom Das
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nutribank.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Executives: short-term approval needed for burst + credit (NutriBank)

Marissa — quick ask for exec approval. NutriBank (D-87921) is currently hitting reserved pool ceiling due to an unexpected workload spike plus a coincident kernel rollout that reduced effective headroom. Priyom recommends opening burst capacity and enabling controlled routing to fallback models.

Proposed immediate ask: approve 4 hours of burst nodes (est. incremental cost $2.4k) and an operational credit of $6k to offset customer impact for the billing cycle. This preserves customer UX while we remediate and backfill the pool.

Customer impact: checkout latency >3x and intermittent checkout failures since 07:50 PDT. NutriBank has high visibility into their customers — we should move fast.

If approved I will notify NutriBank and execute the plan with SRE.

— Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nutribank.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary & proposed mitigation — NutriBank reserved throughput regression

Marissa — summary and recommended course for exec decision:

Timeline:
- 07:45 PDT 4/28: partial kernel rollout to a subset of reserved nodes.
- 07:50 PDT 4/28: customer traffic spike coincides; queue depth increases, 5xx spike.
- 08:40 PDT 4/28: SRE triage confirms GPU pool effectively saturated; autoscaler blocked by reservation policy.

Impact: 60–75% of NutriBank checkout traffic saw >2x latency; error rate peaked at ~18% on checkout route. Estimated lost transactions in the window ~2.1k.

Recommended immediate actions (we can start now upon approval):
1) Approve temporary burst capacity for 4 hours (estimated incremental cost $2.4k).
2) Apply emergency rate-limit on checkout-api to 60% of normal burst RPS to stabilize queues.
3) Route 20% of traffic to smaller-preferred model variant for 30 minutes while cache warms.
4) Post-incident: prep SLA amendment addendum to cover predictable burst allowances and update our kernel rollout gating for reserved pools.

I have drafted the SLA amendment (link in related_links) and attached the proposed document (sla-amendment-proposal-draft.docx). If you approve the burst + credit ask Jordan proposed, we will implement steps 1–3 and schedule a leadership readout with NutriBank CTO tomorrow.

Attachments: sla-amendment-proposal-draft.docx

— Aditya Rao
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nutribank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec summary & proposed mitigation — NutriBank reserved throughput regression

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear timeline and the proposed actions. NutriBank accepts the temporary burst while your team stabilizes traffic; please confirm exact ETA to fully restore normal latencies and the plan for the customer credit. Also requesting a short postmortem and mitigation commitments (kernel rollout gating for reserved pools).

We will plan to have our CTO join the readout tomorrow at 11:00 PDT — please send invites.

— Elena
